title: The Handoff Tax: Swapping Models Mid-Run in Coding Agents
hook: Escalating a struggling coding agent to a stronger model recovers less than half the quality gap while costing a premium. Downshifting, oddly, is the good deal.
key_points: Long coding-agent runs tempt you to swap models mid-trajectory: escalate when stuck, downshift once the hard reasoning is done.
Each swap forces the receiving model to continue a non-native trajectory written by a different model.
Across Claude and GPT pairs, full-trajectory escalation recovered under half the weak-to-strong quality gap at a substantial cost premium — the handoff tax.
Downshifting from the strong to the cheap model gave a favorable cost-quality point instead.
The best interface reverses with direction: trim the weak model's trajectory when escalating, keep the strong model's when downshifting.
Repository state was preserved across handoffs, so the effect comes from inherited trajectory context, not lost work.
content_html: Coding agents now run for dozens of model calls, tool uses, and edits, which makes model choice a mid-run decision rather than a setup flag. Ganz and colleagues studied what actually happens when you switch: escalate to a stronger, pricier model when a cheap one is floundering, or downshift once the hard reasoning is over. Either way, the receiving model has to continue a non-native trajectory someone else wrote.
extra_html: Using low-cost/low-capability and high-cost/high-capability pairs from the Claude and GPT families, the authors varied handoff direction, timing, and interface — full-trajectory transfer, compaction, or trajectory removal — while keeping the repository state intact. Across both families, full-trajectory escalation recovered less than half of the weak-to-strong quality gap and still charged a substantial cost premium; they name this penalty the handoff tax. Downshift, by contrast, sat at a favorable cost-quality point. The most useful practical detail is that the preferred interface flips with direction: giving the receiver less of the weak model's trajectory improved escalation, while stripping the strong model's trajectory made downshift worse. Full setup and numbers are in the paper on arXiv.

related.title: Failure as a Process: An Anatomy of CLI Coding Agent Trajectories
related.hook: A 3,843-trajectory autopsy of coding agents finds most failures aren't slips — they're wrong beliefs formed in the first few steps, invisible until it's too late to recover.

related.title: Token Budgets: When Agents Burn Money
related.hook: A single retry loop can spend thousands of dollars before anyone notices. This paper catalogs 63 real budget-overrun incidents — and asks the type system to make over-spending a compile error.

related.title: Model Routing Is Simple. Until It Isn't.
related.hook: Picking the 'right' model per query looks like classification. IBM Research argues it's really a systems-optimization problem — and treating it as less costs money and speed.

flashcards.prompt: What is the 'handoff tax' in a coding agent run?
flashcards.back_html: The cost-quality penalty paid when one model continues another's trajectory. Full-trajectory escalation to a stronger model recovered less than half the quality gap at a substantial cost premium.

flashcards.prompt: How should the inherited trajectory be handled differently when escalating versus downshifting?

choices.text: Reduce the weak model's trajectory when escalating; keep the strong model's when downshifting
Always pass the full trajectory — more context helps in both directions
Always strip the trajectory and hand over only the repository state

flashcards.explanation_html: The preferred interface reverses with direction: less weak-model trajectory improved escalation quality, while removing the strong model's trajectory hurt downshift quality.

flashcards.prompt: Which switch direction offered the better cost-quality trade-off in this study?

choices.text: Downshifting to the cheaper model once the hard reasoning is done
Escalating to the stronger model as soon as the cheap one struggles
Neither — both directions degraded quality equally

flashcards.explanation_html: Escalation paid the handoff tax, whereas downshift landed at a favorable cost-quality point.
